scope.summary: Author migrations for the four canonical texture-authority tables per Master Spec 13.9 section 6 schema: tailor_uv_islands, tailor_pbr_materials, tailor_graphic_layers, and tailor_material_assignments (supersedes the non-canonical tailor_uv_sets working name).
acceptance_criteria: Four dated migration pairs (YYYY_MM_DD_tailor_<topic>.sql + .down.sql) create tailor_uv_islands, tailor_pbr_materials, tailor_graphic_layers, and tailor_material_assignments exactly per the 13.9 section 6 DDL (TEXT PKs with prefixed uuid_v7 ids, event_ledger_event_id FK on every table).
No table named tailor_uv_sets is created anywhere; the canonical name is tailor_uv_islands.
Up/down migrations run clean in both directions.
proof_targets: sqlx migrate run && sqlx migrate revert (tailor_uv_islands, tailor_pbr_materials, tailor_graphic_layers, tailor_material_assignments)
scope.risk_if_missed: No texture authority means textures cannot be promoted/reused; a tailor_uv_sets table would drift from the canonical 16-table set in 13.14 and break MT-153/MT-233/MT-379 UV validation wiring.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
